last.minutes: We maintain our core spot holdings in BTC, SOL, and AAVE while slightly trimming AAVE to strictly comply with the 30% individual asset limit. In the futures book, we close the NEAR short position to cut losses and avoid fighting the broader risk-on sentiment, moving to a flat stance to preserve capital. This balanced approach protects our portfolio from excessive transaction costs and tax drag while positioning us safely for the current market regime.
notes: scaled the spot book from 95% to 95% invested

futures.why: Closing the NEAR short to cut losses and protect capital from conflicting market signals in a risk-on environment.

spot.why: Retaining strong exposure while trimming slightly to respect the 30% single-coin limit and avoid excessive tax drag.
Leading the 'Uptober' rally with robust institutional inflows and strong ETF demand.
Benefiting from solid volume and ongoing institutional adoption via banking integrations.
Holding current allocation to avoid unnecessary churn and fees while awaiting broader altcoin recovery.

lessons.text: Strictly enforcing concentration limits and rotating out of overcrowded positions protects capital from unexpected liquidation risks.
Strictly adhering to portfolio concentration limits while minimizing unnecessary churn prevents compliance breaches and preserves capital from excessive transaction costs.

Minimizing unnecessary adjustments to profitable spot positions helps avoid triggering the 31.2% tax and high transaction fees, while rebalancing should be reserved primarily for regulatory compliance.
Strictly adhering to portfolio concentration limits prevents compliance breaches and protects capital from excessive risk.

Trimming positions only when necessary for risk compliance, such as enforcing the 30% single-coin limit, prevents regulatory breaches while protecting the portfolio from excessive transaction fees and tax drag.
Strictly adhering to portfolio concentration limits while cutting underperforming leveraged positions protects capital from unnecessary drawdown and tax drag.
